lens: Handling editor, presentation and evidence quality. I opened all 10 PNGs and cross-checked them against results/tables.md, the current CSVs and the code (core.py, exp_lib.py, exp_main.py, exp_real.py, exp_cross2.py). The user's critique is addressed head-on: (1) "you compare categories, not algorithms" and (2) "your figures all overlap into one point".
verdict: MAJOR REVISION. Submitted to a Q1 venue (IEEE T-ASE, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture, Biosystems Engineering, JFR) as it stands, it would most likely be rejected. The user's critique is right, and the problem runs deeper than it looks. Every one of the 16 "baselines" is a rule for choosing one scalar margin lambda on the same greedy boustrophedon planner. So each method is just a point on one shared, monotone curve lambda -> (P(no miss), overlap). The figures collapse for that structural reason; restyling alone cannot fix it. Among the methods that meet the target, the closest competitor ("Scenario approach") differs from CE-U only in the confidence parameter. For a scalar decision, the conformal order statistic ceil((n+1)(1-eps)) is exactly the Campi-Garatti sampling-and-discarding solution with the expected-violation guarantee. I checked this: with n=100 and eps=0.1, CE-U takes the 91st order statistic and scenario(beta=0.01) takes the 97th. The code actually returns the 96th, an off-by-one bug. So the headline "lowest overlap among valid methods" compares a marginal guarantee with a 99%-confidence (PAC) guarantee, and an expert reviewer will call the comparison unfair. On top of that: no named coverage-planning algorithm (Fields2Cover, Oksanen-Visala, Jin-Tang, Hameed 2016) is compared. Three of the four proposed variants give no benefit (CE-A, CE-pair, CE-R, and also fixed-point and weighted calibration). The artifacts disagree with each other: fig3 shows 19/10 fields, tables.md 27/16, the CSVs 60/60, and the report v2 40/40. Fig6(b) is an empty panel. The cost metric is a planned chord ratio that can go negative (-0.21% at 12 m). The only real execution data is a teleoperated-scale orchard robot with about 0.8 m certified margin (36% overlap), and out-of-distribution validity fails in 3/10 splits. The theory is clean and the problem is novel and relevant, so the paper can be saved. Doing so needs: (i) a two-level comparison, with named planning algorithms x named uncertainty-handling algorithms, matched guarantees, and fair tuning; (ii) experiments in the regimes where CE actually differs from scenario/SAA: multi-dimensional plan families such as per-gap margins and heading, decision-dependent pass counts, field-size and regional shift, and risk control; (iii) a rebuilt figure set: log-scale risk, per-field paired differences, one frontier per plan family, calibration curves, miss-frequency maps; (iv) one consistent, regenerated set of artifacts. In this environment, about 2-3 weeks of focused work.

major_issues.issue: The comparison is between categories of margin rules, not algorithms. All 16 baselines plus CE-U pick one scalar lambda on the same greedy planner (exp_main.py builds one dict `lam` and calls core.plan with it). Every method is therefore a point on one curve lambda -> (P, overlap) per field. Among methods that meet the target, CE-U is identical in kind to the Campi-Garatti scenario approach with discarding: for d=1 the conformal quantile is the sampling-and-discarding solution with E[V] <= (k+1)/(n+1). The 'Scenario approach' baseline differs only because it asks for a PAC guarantee (beta=0.01). Verified: n=100, eps=0.1 gives CE-U = 91st order statistic, valid scenario = 97th, and code returns the 96th (off-by-one).
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: A reviewer who knows conformal prediction or scenario optimization will say that the claimed gain (6.6% vs 7.9-9.2% overlap) comes from comparing a marginal guarantee with a 99%-confidence guarantee, and that 'CE-U' is a known order statistic. That reads as no methodological novelty plus an unfair baseline, which is a standard reject reason. A robotics reviewer will separately say that no competing planning algorithm was tested, only parameters of one planner.
major_issues.concrete_fix: (1) Add a proposition stating that for scalar lambda, CE-U is the same as scenario-with-discarding under the expectation guarantee, and CE-PAC (training-conditional, Vovk 2012, delta=0.01) is the same as scenario(beta=0.01). Report matched-guarantee pairs side by side and say they coincide. (2) Move the claimed advantage to the places where conformal really differs. (a) Plan families with d>1 decisions: per-gap margins, per-pass sigma_k, heading. There the scenario approach needs about n >= 2(d+ln(1/beta))/eps runs (about 700 for d=30), while CE stays valid with n=20-100 because it calibrates a 1-D family through a score. (b) Decision-dependent pass counts (Thm 2/3). (c) Field-size and regional shift. (d) Risk control (Thm 4). (3) Restructure the experiments as a two-factor design: planning algorithm (F2C-style angle optimization, Hameed-2016 terrain spacing, CE-heading) x uncertainty-handling algorithm (CE, scenario d=N, SAA-MILP, conformal robust optimization, Wasserstein-DRO chance constraint, GEV, GP-Bayes). Show the results as one frontier curve per plan family, so different algorithms produce different curves rather than points on one curve.
major_issues.effort: 2-3 days. All pieces run on the existing simulator. The per-gap SAA MILP fits scipy.optimize.milp (scipy 1.18 is installed). Re-running main v3 takes about 20 s per field on 4 CPUs.

major_issues.issue: No named coverage-path-planning algorithm is compared, even though agricultural Q1 reviewers will expect it. Missing: Fields2Cover angle optimization, Oksanen-Visala, Jin-Tang 3D-terrain heading, Hameed et al. 2016 side-to-side 3D skip/overlap minimization, and ISO 12188-2 spec-based overlap. The driving direction is frozen to the harvester heading mode, so terrain-aware planning cannot show its value.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Reviewers at CEA, Biosystems Engineering and JFR routinely ask for comparison with state-of-the-art open-source CPP (Fields2Cover is the standard). Hameed et al. (RAS 2016) explicitly targets skip/overlap between swaths on 3D terrain, so leaving it out looks like an unacknowledged prior-art gap.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Treat CE as a plug-in certification layer and demonstrate it on top of 3 planners. (a) Fields2Cover: the PyPI sdist fields2cover-2.1.0 downloads, but it needs GDAL>=3.0, TinyXML2, Eigen3 and swig, and gdal-config/swig are absent here. So re-implement F2C's brute-force swath-angle search (objectives: number of swaths / swath length) in shapely, and validate it against F2C's own unit-test fields from the GitHub repo. (b) Hameed 2016 terrain-compensated spacing (w*cos(side slope) from the DEM). (c) Jin-Tang-style slope-aware heading. For each planner report 'default overlap rule' vs '+CE'. Add a TUNED fixed overlap (one value per region chosen on the 20 training fields to reach 90%), which is what a practitioner would actually do, and an ORACLE lambda* per field (the (1-eps) quantile of 2000 test-run scores) as a lower bound.
major_issues.effort: 2-4 days (F2C-style re-implementation ~1 day, Hameed/Jin-Tang rules ~0.5 day, re-runs ~1 day).

major_issues.issue: The artifacts are stale, inconsistent and partly broken. fig3_main is titled '19 real fields' (paddy) / '10' (wheat); tables.md says 27/16; main_*_v3.csv contain 60/60 (commit dffd521 'Final results'); experiments_report.md describes v2 with 40/40 fields, 11 methods and Wilcoxon p=0.23/0.69, while tables.md gives p=0.41/0.90. Fig6 panel (b) is empty axes. Fig6(a) plots QR-GBM at about 0.835, but the table says 0.756 and the current cross2_paddy.csv gives 0.792. Fig3 overlap labels (e.g. CE-pair 11.2) do not match the table (11.4). Fig2(a) says n=246/250 fields, while the report says 137/162 used and main uses 60/60.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: An empty panel and numbers that disagree between figures and tables suggest cherry-picking or carelessness. Editors return such papers without review, and reviewers stop trusting every other number.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Write one make_all.py that reads only the final CSVs, regenerates tables.md and every figure, and asserts that field counts, method lists and summary values agree across outputs (it fails loudly otherwise). Write the CSV SHA256 into the figure metadata. Rewrite experiments_report.md from the regenerated tables. Delete the obsolete v2 numbers from the text.

major_issues.issue: The main result figure collapses. 7 of 17 methods sit at P≈0, the valid ones are squeezed into 0.9-1.0 on a linear 0-1 axis, CE-U and CE-A overlap exactly, and mean±CI bars hide per-field behaviour. Verified from the CSVs: CE-A and CE-U produce the SAME number of passes in 48/60 paddy and 42/60 wheat fields. CE-U and scenario produce the same pass count in 30/60 and 26/60 fields (median gain 1.1 / 2.5 overlap points). Gaussian-on-score adds up to +63 passes and CVaR up to +48 on single fields; this cost-tail instability is CE's best visible selling point, and it is hidden. Among valid methods P(miss) ranges from 0.0065 to 0.084, more than a decade, so a log axis separates them.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Reviewers cannot see any difference between the proposed variants, and the main figure shows only that straw men fail, which is not informative. 'Figures where methods overlap into one point' is exactly the user's concern and a common reviewer complaint.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Rebuild Fig. 3 as follows (details in figure_issues). (a) A reliability-cost plane: log P(miss) vs executed overlap or Δpasses per ha, with 2-D hierarchical-bootstrap CIs, one frontier curve per PLAN FAMILY (calibrators appear as ticks on the curve), and the failing methods compressed into one labelled band. (b) Per-field paired Δpasses vs CE-U on a symlog axis (beeswarm with median and Hodges-Lehmann CI). (c) The ECDF of per-field realized coverage, with the theoretical CE distribution Beta(l, n+1-l) ⊗ Binomial(300) shaded. Keep at most 2 straw men in the main figure (tuned fixed overlap, pointwise conformal as the 'no-sup' ablation) and move the rest to the supplement.
major_issues.effort: 1-2 days (all panels except the frontier curves can be built from existing CSVs; the frontiers need the lambda-sweep in the next issues).

major_issues.issue: The cost metric is wrong and insufficient. exp_lib.overlap_ratio = Σ w·chord(M, y_k)/area(M) − 1 is a PLANNED quantity, not executed overlap. It can be negative (sens.csv: −0.21% at 12 m width), ignores overhang beyond the boundary, and is quantized by integer pass counts. The proposal defines J = ∫(multiplicity−1)_+, which the code never computes. The units ‱ (per ten thousand) are unusual in agricultural engineering.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: A negative overlap is physically impossible and makes the main cost axis look untrustworthy. Agricultural-engineering reviewers will want executed double-coverage, pass count, path or time, and input savings per hectare.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Extend core.evaluate. It already sorts the executed intervals per cross-section, so add the multiplicity integral (Σ interval lengths − union length) to get executed overlap per run. Report: executed overlap %, passes, Δpasses/ha, path length including Dubins headland turns, operating time at 2 m/s, and missed area in m²/ha. Put Δpasses/ha and time in the abstract instead of the overlap percentage. Use the integer structure deliberately: after choosing N, spread the leftover slack evenly. That costs nothing and raises P at the same N.
major_issues.effort: 0.5-1 day, plus re-runs (~1 h per crop).

major_issues.issue: Real-world evidence is weak and partly contradicts the claims. The main experiments are simulated with literature-level parameters. The CitrusFarm Jackal is likely manually or teleoperated (verify in Teng et al. 2023), and its certified margin is about 0.8 m (36% overlap with a virtual 6 m implement), roughly 30x RTK autosteer error. References are a least-squares-fitted row lattice, so tree-row irregularity counts as 'error'. In leave-one-block/day-out (OOD) splits, CE-U falls below 0.9 in 3/10 cases (K=5, 13D: 0.833), shown with no CIs. CE-pair and CE-U give identical numbers on the robot (0.916 / 36.3%), which looks like a degenerate case or a bug.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: 'Certified' while 30% of real held-out splits fail, plus a 36% overlap that no farmer would accept, invites a reject for lacking practical validity. Reviewers will say simulation results do not transfer.
major_issues.concrete_fix: (1) Put Clopper-Pearson CIs and a one-sided binomial test vs 0.9 on each LOBO/LODO split. With n_test of about 30-130 windows, several 'failures' may be within noise; say so with numbers. (2) Run the shift-aware variants (weighted CE, CE-pair, CE-PAC, ACI) on these exact splits and show which ones restore validity. (3) Present the robot study as a 'different error regime' stress test, and report overlap relative to competitors and relative to the oracle, not as an absolute number. (4) Check simulator realism: compare simulated pass-to-pass error quantiles with ISO 12188-2-style published autosteer test values. (5) Look for real autosteer executions on reachable hosts: AgOpenGPS field folders on GitHub (recorded section coverage; unverified lead), and estimate pass spacing directly from the 250 harvester GNSS trajectories if their accuracy permits. (6) Explain or fix the CE-pair = CE-U identity.
major_issues.effort: 1 day for CIs/tests and variants on existing splits; 2-4 days for the data search and realism check (feasibility depends on what is found).

major_issues.issue: Three of the four 'ours' variants, and two of the theorems, have no empirical payoff. CE-A shows no gain (p=0.41/0.90; identical plans in 70-80% of fields). CE-pair is strictly more conservative than CE-U (11.4% vs 6.6%). CE-R appears in the P(no miss) table at 0.001, a category error, and is about 4.5x conservative because B/(n+1) = 1/501 ≈ 0.002 is two-thirds of alpha = 0.003. Fixed-point calibration makes no difference even in the hard regime (ablation_hard: 0.921 vs 0.918). Weighted CP gives no benefit.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Four theorems but one useful variant suggests the theory is decorative. A reviewer will ask why Thm 2-4 exist if naive split conformal does just as well everywhere.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Test each component in the regime it was designed for, or demote it to the appendix. (a) CE-A: let the heading vary, since side slope depends on heading, and optimize the heading for the certified pass count. Add a direction-aware residual model: the simulator's antenna-roll offset h·sin(roll)(1−c) flips sign with travel direction, so adjacent gaps alternately open and close, and conformalizing residuals around a slope×direction bias model should cut erosion on hilly fields. Plot gain vs within-field heterogeneity. (b) CE-pair: a FIELD-SIZE SHIFT experiment (calibrate on small fields, deploy on large ones). Pooled sup-score coverage should decay like about 0.9^(N_test/N_cal), while the union bound scales with N, which gives CE-pair a reason to exist. (c) Fixed point: calibrate on the nominal plan for a narrow implement (1.5 m) or GNSS×3, where N(q)/N_ref is large. (d) CE-R: an alpha-sweep from 1e-4 to 1e-2 on log-log axes against Learn-then-Test and SAA-on-mean, showing where the B/(n+1) term dominates. Remove CE-R from the P(no miss) table.
major_issues.effort: 3-5 days in total; each sub-experiment is under 1 day of compute.

major_issues.issue: Statistical reporting is not credible. The [0.911, 0.923]-style intervals are pooled Clopper-Pearson over fields×300 runs; they ignore clustering by field and by calibration draw, so they are far too narrow. Every Holm p-value is the floor value (2.4e-07 / 4.9e-04), which carries no information. 'Fields not significantly below target' (89%/100%) is never compared with what theory predicts. Means are taken over feasible fields only, which biases them.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Statistically literate reviewers will flag pseudo-replication and uninformative p-values.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Use a two-level (field, calibration draw) bootstrap for all CIs. Replace the p-value column with paired effect sizes: median Δpasses/ha and Δoverlap with Hodges-Lehmann 95% CI, plus the fraction of fields where CE is strictly cheaper. Compare the per-field coverage distribution with the predicted Beta⊗Binomial; 18-23% of fields below 0.9 is consistent with theory, so say it. Code infeasible fields as +∞ cost in rank-based tests, and report the infeasibility count separately. Use a non-inferiority test for validity (H0: P < 1−ε−0.02).

major_issues.issue: The validity evidence is thin and partly contradicts Thm 1's tightness claim. In fig5, CE-U reaches 0.775 at target 0.70 and 0.852 at 0.80, well above the stated band [1−ε, 1−ε+1/(n+1)] (width about 0.01). Only one competitor is shown, on only 12 fields × 4 draws. The ε grid stops at 0.05, which is exactly where heavy-tailed RTK data should make Gaussian methods anti-conservative, the most persuasive contrast available.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Unexplained over-coverage undermines the 'exact and tight' story, and a calibration plot with one baseline is not a comparison.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Use Lemma 1's iff condition for 'score-based evaluation': P(no miss | λ) is approximately P(S_test ≤ λ), using test-run scores at a reference plan. That gives dense calibration curves for EVERY method at ε ∈ {0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5}, nearly for free; then spot-check 3 points by direct simulation. Decompose the slack into Lemma-1 sufficiency (4.5%), fixed-point domination and integer-pass slack. Raise n_cal to 200-500 for ε ≤ 0.02.

major_issues.issue: Competitor implementations and tuning are not fair. Scenario has an off-by-one (returns s[k+1] instead of s[k]; verified 96 vs 97). The Wasserstein radius ρ = sd·sqrt(log(1/β)/n) is ad hoc, which produces 82% overlap on the robot, an obvious straw man. 'Empirical pointwise quantile' and 'Pointwise conformal' are duplicates (both λ=0.0224). CVaR is the Nemirovski-Shapiro convex approximation but is not named as such. No method's hyperparameters are tuned.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Reviewers who see untuned or buggy baselines discount the whole comparison.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Fix the scenario index. Choose the DRO radius by K-fold CV on training fields, as Esfahani-Kuhn recommend, and also show its full radius sweep. Drop the duplicate pointwise methods. Name every method by algorithm and citation. Document the tuning protocol: hyperparameters chosen on the 20 training fields only, applied unchanged to evaluation fields.

major_issues.issue: The online/drift study is a single synthetic linear-moisture ramp with only ACI vs static. On the real stream, 49 strips with about 3 misses cannot measure a 0.10 rate, and static has 0 misses at 41% overlap.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: ACI from 2021 alone is outdated as an online baseline, and one trajectory gives no variance.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Add DtACI (Gibbs-Candès 2024), conformal PID (Angelopoulos et al. 2023), rolling-window and exponentially weighted split conformal (nexCP, Barber et al. 2023), and conformal decision theory (Lekeufack et al. 2024). Run ≥20 seeds × 6 fields, show bands, add a stationary control segment, and report long-run frequency with CI and mean λ_t. On the real stream, bootstrap over block orderings.

major_issues.issue: Positioning is missing against the closest conformal and planning literature: Conformal Predictive Programming (Zhao et al. 2024), conformal planning (Lindemann et al. 2023), feedback-covariate-shift conformal (Fannjiang et al. 2022, very close to Thm 3), conformal robust optimization (Johnstone-Cox 2021; Patel et al. 2024), and Hameed et al. 2016. The simulator also ignores the 3-D projection of swath width on side slopes (w·cos θ), which is the effect Hameed 2016 corrects.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: 'Is CE just CPP applied to swaths?' is the first question a conformal reviewer will ask; the 3-D omission is the first an agricultural reviewer will ask.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Add a related-work comparison table (decision dimension, guarantee type, decision dependence, shift, online). Run CPP and conformal-RO as competitors (see competitor list). Add the w·cos θ projection to evaluation and planner.

major_issues.issue: Presentation hygiene. Chinese and English are mixed in the tables. Method names differ across artifacts ('Scenario approach' / 'Scenario (Campi-Garatti)'; 'Robust worst-case' / 'Worst-case (max score)'; 'Gaussian chance constr.' / 'Gaussian on score'). The method order and colour mapping change between figures. All baselines are the same grey, so ten methods cannot be told apart. Titles sit inside figures. Fonts differ (fig_example). ‱ is used as a unit.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: It signals an unfinished manuscript and makes cross-figure reading impossible.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Fix one method registry (name, citation, family, colour, marker, order) used by every script. Use a colour-blind-safe palette by family (conformal = blues, scenario/PAC = greens, CVaR/DRO = oranges, parametric = purples, heuristics = greys) and distinct markers within each family. Export vector PDFs at journal column widths (88/180 mm) with 7-8 pt fonts. Use English only, and m²/ha or % for missed area.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Fields2Cover swath-angle optimization + boustrophedon/snake route (planning layer)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: The PyPI sdist fields2cover-2.1.0 is reachable but needs GDAL>=3.0, TinyXML2, Eigen3 and swig, which are absent. Re-implement its BruteForce angle search (rotate the polygon 0-179° in 1° steps; objectives N_swaths and total swath length) in shapely, and validate against the unit-test fields in the GitHub repo. Run 'F2C + default/tuned overlap' vs 'F2C + CE'.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Mier, Valente, de Bruin, IEEE RA-L 8(4), 2023

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Side-to-side 3D coverage planning that minimizes skip/overlap between swaths on terrain
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Compute the terrain-projected spacing w·cos(side slope) per pass from the Copernicus DEM (already loaded in Field.gy_map). Use it as a named deterministic competitor and as a planner that CE plugs into.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Hameed, la Cour-Harbo, Osen, Robotics and Autonomous Systems 76, 2016 (verify pages)

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Slope-aware driving-direction optimization on 3D terrain
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Choose the heading that minimizes mean |side slope| and turns (Jin-Tang cost) from the DEM, then compare with CE-heading (heading chosen to minimize the CERTIFIED pass count using the σ̂(slope) model). This is where CE-A can show a real gain.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Jin & Tang, J. Field Robotics 28(3), 2011; Jin & Tang, Trans. ASABE 53(1), 2010

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Trapezoidal decomposition + merging CPP for field machines
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Needed only for non-convex fields. Use the raw (non-hull) DBSCAN field outlines, decompose, and apply CE per cell. Shows CE works beyond convex hulls.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: ISO 12188-2 spec-based overlap (industry practice)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: overlap = 2 × published 95% pass-to-pass accuracy of RTK autosteer (e.g. ±2.5 cm), plus a tuned fixed overlap chosen on training fields to reach 90%. These replace the untuned 5/10 cm rules.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: ISO 12188-2:2012, Tractors and machinery for agriculture and forestry, test procedures for positioning and guidance systems, Part 2

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Chance-constrained sample average approximation (SAA) with per-gap margins
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Decision m_k for each of the N-1 gaps plus 2 boundaries. MILP: min Σ m_k s.t. diff_k^i ≤ m_k + M·z_i, Σ z_i ≤ ⌊ε n⌋, z binary. scipy.optimize.milp (HiGHS), n=100 scenarios, about 30 gaps: seconds per field. Shows multi-dimensional optimization without finite-sample validity.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Luedtke & Ahmed, SIAM J. Optim. 19(2), 2008; Pagnoncelli, Ahmed, Shapiro, JOTA 142, 2009

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Scenario approach with d = N decision variables (per-gap margins), plus the matched-guarantee scalar version
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Per-gap margins = max over retained scenarios after greedy discarding; violation bound from Campi-Garatti with d=N. Shows the sample size needed grows with d while CE does not. Also report scalar scenario with the expectation guarantee (equal to CE-U) and with beta=0.01 (equal to CE-PAC), after fixing the off-by-one in exp_lib.scenario_lambda.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Campi & Garatti, SIAM J. Optim. 19(3), 2008; Campi & Garatti, JOTA 148(2), 2011

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Conformal Predictive Programming (a-priori and a-posteriori variants)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: A-posteriori: solve the SAA per-gap MILP on n1=50 runs, then conformally rescale the margin vector on n2=50 runs. A-priori: a conformal constraint on the sup score. This is the closest conformal competitor, and the paper must say how CE differs.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Zhao, Yu, Deshmukh, Lindemann, arXiv:2402.07407, 2024 (venue unverified)

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Conformal uncertainty sets for robust optimization (box/ellipsoid over the per-gap deviation vector)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Calibrate a normalized box set {max_k diff_k/s_k ≤ q} or an ellipsoid with a Mahalanobis score on the vector of per-gap maxima. Robust margin per gap = support function of the set. A few dozen lines.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Johnstone & Cox, PMLR (COPA) 152, 2021; Patel, Rayan, Tewari, AISTATS 2024 (verify)

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Wasserstein-DRO chance constraint (exact/CVaR reformulation, CV-tuned radius)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Replace the ad-hoc rho with the exact reformulation for a scalar or per-gap linear constraint, and choose the radius by K-fold CV on training fields. Show the full radius-sweep curve.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Xie, Math. Prog. 186, 2021; Chen, Kuhn, Wiesemann, Operations Research 72(1), 2024; Mohajerin Esfahani & Kuhn, Math. Prog. 171, 2018

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: CVaR convex approximation of the chance constraint (correctly named)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Already present as 'CVaR (empirical)'. Rename it and cite. Add its ε-sweep to the calibration plot.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Nemirovski & Shapiro, SIAM J. Optim. 17(4), 2006; Rockafellar & Uryasev, J. Risk 2000

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Extreme-value (GEV / peaks-over-threshold) quantile of the sup score
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: The score is a maximum, so GEV is the principled parametric alternative. Fit scipy.stats.genextreme to the calibration scores and take the (1-ε) quantile. Expected to look good at ε=0.1 and to be fragile at small n or ε.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Coles, An Introduction to Statistical Modeling of Extreme Values, Springer 2001

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Gaussian-process Bayesian error model with posterior-predictive chance constraint
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: sklearn GaussianProcessRegressor on pass-to-pass differences with features (side slope, direction parity, along-track s). Jointly sample N passes from the posterior to estimate P(sup ≤ λ), then pick λ. This is the uncalibrated 'learned uncertainty' competitor the proposal promised (§8.4).
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Rasmussen & Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, MIT Press 2006

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Tube-MPC / robust-invariant-set margin (control-side worst case)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: For the LQR-I closed loop, compute an outer approximation of the minimal robust positively invariant set under a disturbance bound estimated from calibration (max RTK + slip). Erosion = tube half-width. A named control-theory competitor and the 'coupling' the proposal claims.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Conditional / Mondrian conformal by slope bin or direction parity
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Group-conditional quantiles per slope tercile or per (up→down, down→up) gap type, as the competitor for CE-A. Group-conditional coverage via Gibbs-Cherian-Candès is an optional extension.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Vovk et al., Algorithmic Learning in a Random World 2005 (Mondrian); Gibbs, Cherian, Candès, arXiv:2305.12616 (journal version unverified)

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Feedback-covariate-shift conformal (decision-dependent shift)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: The plan determines the feature distribution, which is the same structure as Thm 3. Implement their weighted quantile with plan-induced likelihood ratios, compare with the fixed-point CE, and cite as the closest theory.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Fannjiang, Bates, Angelopoulos, Listgarten, Jordan, PNAS 119(43), 2022

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Learn-then-Test and SAA-on-mean (competitors for the risk certificate CE-R)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: LTT: test a λ grid with Hoeffding-Bentkus p-values and fixed-sequence FWER control on the surrogate loss already computed in exp_lib.risk_lambda. SAA: smallest λ with empirical mean loss ≤ α. Run the α-sweep on log-log axes.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Angelopoulos, Bates, Candès, Jordan, Lei, Learn then Test, arXiv:2110.01052 (journal version unverified); Angelopoulos et al., Conformal Risk Control, ICLR 2024

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Online competitors to ACI: DtACI, conformal PID, nexCP / rolling window, conformal decision theory
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Each is about 20-50 lines on the existing λ_t loop in exp_real.py / exp_sens.py --part aci. Use ≥20 seeds with bands.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Gibbs & Candès, JMLR 25, 2024; Angelopoulos, Candès, Tibshirani, NeurIPS 2023; Barber et al., Ann. Statist. 51(2), 2023; Lekeufack et al., ICRA 2024

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: PAC / training-conditional conformal (Wilks tolerance limit)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Order statistic chosen by binomial so that P(coverage ≥ 1-ε) ≥ 1-δ. The matched-guarantee partner of scenario(beta). Reported as the 'CE-PAC' option, also a remedy for the per-field shortfalls.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Vovk, Conditional validity of inductive conformal predictors, ACML 2012 / Machine Learning 2013; Wilks, Ann. Math. Stat. 12, 1941
